comparison: Perfect agreement on claims C1-C8 regarding NPR-15's role in pathogen resistance. Both evaluations find the evidence from multiple alleles, pathogens, and experimental approaches strongly convincing. OpenEval emphasizes the convergence of independent methods, while peer reviewers highlight the rigor and elegance of the work.

Complete concordance on claims C10-C18 regarding pathogen avoidance behavior. Both evaluations support the behavioral assays and oxygen manipulation experiments. OpenEval specifically notes the distinction from NPR-1/aerotaxis mechanisms, while peer reviewers praise the elegant approaches and independence from aerotaxis.

Full agreement on claims C20-C21 and C24 regarding control experiments. Both evaluations accept these as appropriate negative controls ruling out alternative explanations. OpenEval emphasizes their role in strengthening causal interpretation, while peer reviewers acknowledge they appropriately rule out pharyngeal pumping and defecation effects.

Strong agreement on claims C27-C35 regarding transcriptomic analysis. Both evaluations find the RNA-seq, bioinformatic analyses, and qRT-PCR validation convincing. OpenEval notes minor speculation about ELT-2's 'major role' without functional validation, while peer reviewers express no such reservations and fully endorse the transcriptomic approach.

Complete concordance on claims C36-C41 regarding genetic epistasis with ELT-2 and HLH-30. Both evaluations strongly support the epistasis data and pathway identification. OpenEval highlights the complete vs. partial suppression patterns, while peer reviewers praise the use of multiple strains and genetic approaches.

Perfect agreement on claims C42-C51 regarding ASJ neuron identification for immunity. Both evaluations find the convergence of expression data, tissue-specific RNAi, rescue experiments, and ablation studies compelling. OpenEval notes intermediate phenotypes in some ablation strains, while peer reviewers emphasize the elegant use of diverse mutant strains and genetic methods.

Strong agreement on claims C52-C58 regarding independence of avoidance from immune genes. Both evaluations accept the systematic RNAi screening results. OpenEval expresses slight concern that the conclusion of complete independence (C58) may be overstated due to potential functional redundancy, while peer reviewers fully accept the independence conclusion without reservations.

Complete concordance on claims C59-C63 regarding ASJ neuron control of avoidance behavior. Both evaluations strongly support the neuronal localization using rescue, ablation, and cell-specific approaches. OpenEval emphasizes the specificity for ASJ, while peer reviewers highlight this as a central, well-supported discovery using genetic ablation methods.

Full agreement on claims C65-C71 regarding GON-2 as downstream effector of avoidance. Both evaluations support the genetic analysis, tissue-specific RNAi localizing GON-2 to intestine, and epistasis experiments. OpenEval emphasizes the connection between neuronal NPR-15 and intestinal GON-2, while peer reviewers note the successful implication of gut signaling pathways.

Strong agreement on claims C72-C78 regarding the integrative model of dual NPR-15 function. Both evaluations endorse the model showing ASJ neurons controlling both immunity (via ELT-2/HLH-30) and avoidance (via GON-2). OpenEval treats this as the key conceptual advance, while peer reviewers emphasize its significance for understanding neural resource utilization and GPCR regulation of immunity.

OpenEval evaluated 29 literature citation claims (C9, C19, C22-C23, C55, C64, C67, C75, C79, C82-C89, C91, C104-C108, C110-C115, C117, C119) as appropriately contextualizing prior work. No corresponding peer review evaluation specifically addresses these citation claims.

Partial overlap on claims C25-C26 regarding NPR-15's dual role in immunity and behavior. OpenEval groups these with 17 other summary/interpretation claims and notes some speculation about evolutionary rationale. Peer reviewers (R4) explicitly endorse C25-C26 as a central, well-supported integrative conclusion about NPR-15 mediating both molecular and behavioral immune responses, with no concerns about speculation.
